chapter.title: Edible Vegetables and Certain Roots and Tubers

page.h1: HTS Chapter 07: Edible Vegetables and Certain Roots and Tubers — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: What Canada, Mexico, EU, Japan & China Charge on U.S. Vegetables
seo.shortDescription: Tariffs on U.S. vegetables, potatoes and pulses in 2026, market by market: 0% in Canada and Mexico, 30% on yellow peas in India, about 42–48% on pulses in China.
keywords: india tariff on us yellow peas

intro: What each large market charges on U.S. vegetables, potatoes and pulses in 2026, next to what the U.S. shipped there in 2025; the EU counts as one market because its members share one tariff. India is added at the end, although it bought only $6.7 million in 2025, because its yellow-pea duty is one of the few tariff increases on these goods since 2025. For most of the trade the tariff is zero: Canada and Mexico under USMCA, the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica under CAFTA-DR (except Costa Rica’s potato and onion quotas), and the EU on pulses and, since July 2026, on many vegetables. Japan charges nothing on most U.S. potatoes, onions and frozen vegetables. Taiwan (15–25% on fresh vegetables), China and India cost real money. For fresh vegetables, the buyer’s plant-health rules usually decide whether a product can be sold at all.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

profile.headline: Canada takes 59% of U.S. vegetable exports (lettuce, peppers, broccoli and cauliflower, tomatoes, onions) and charges nothing on them under CUSMA. Its 2025 counter-tariff hit U.S. tomatoes and fresh beans from March 4 to August 31, 2025; its September 2026 counter-tariffs skip vegetables.

regulator.name: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
regulator.requirement: The importer needs a Safe Food for Canadians licence. CFIA’s Automated Import Reference System (AIRS) sets the plant-health conditions for each vegetable and U.S. origin, including when a USDA phytosanitary certificate is needed.

profile.headline: Mexico is the second-largest buyer, led by dry beans and other pulses ($210 million) and fresh potatoes ($108 million), all duty-free under USMCA. Since May 2022 U.S. fresh potatoes can be sold throughout Mexico, not just within 26 km of the border.

regulator.name: SENASICA (National Service of Agro-Alimentary Health, Safety and Quality)
regulator.requirement: SENASICA sets the phytosanitary import requirement for each product and origin; fresh potatoes, vegetables and pulses are inspected at entry against it, usually with a USDA phytosanitary certificate.

markets.name: European Union
markets.rule: EU Common Customs Tariff with the 2026 preferences for U.S. goods (Regulation (EU) 2026/1455)

0701.rate: 0% on paper; U.S. potatoes are not admitted
0701.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: ware potatoes (0701 90 50, 0701 90 90) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal rate 11.5%). But Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072, Annex VI (entries 15 and 17), prohibits potato tubers from the United States, so the preference cannot be used.

0702.rate: % duty removed; any entry-price duty remains
0702.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex II: the 8.8% ad valorem part of the duty on tomatoes is suspended to zero for U.S. goods from July 1, 2026; the specific duty that applies when the import price is below the entry price is kept.

0703.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: onions other than sets (0703 10 19) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal rate 9.6%). Garlic, shallots and leeks keep the normal rate.

0704.basis: EU Common Customs Tariff, 2026 (TARIC, origin US): cauliflower and broccoli (0704 10 00) 13.6% (minimum €1.60/100 kg) in season, otherwise 12%. Not in the 2026/1455 annexes.

0705.basis: EU Common Customs Tariff, 2026 (TARIC, origin US): head lettuce (0705 11 00) 12% (minimum €2/100 kg/br) from April to November, other lettuce (0705 19 00) 10.4%. Not in the 2026/1455 annexes.

0706.basis: EU Common Customs Tariff, 2026 (TARIC, origin US): carrots and turnips (0706 10 00) 13.6%. Not in the 2026/1455 annexes.

0707.rate: % duty removed; any entry-price duty remains
0707.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex II: the 12.8% ad valorem part of the duty on cucumbers (0707 00 05) is suspended to zero for U.S. goods; the entry-price specific duty is kept.

0708.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: fresh or chilled beans (0708 20 00) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal rate 10.4%, minimum €1.60/100 kg in season). Fresh peas keep the normal rate.

0709.rate: Asparagus and sweet peppers 0%; others normal rate
0709.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: asparagus (0709 20 00, normal 10.2%) and sweet peppers (0709 60 10, normal 7.2%) 0% from July 1, 2026; Annex II removes the % duty on globe artichokes and courgettes. Celery (12.8%) and most other fresh vegetables keep the normal rate.

0710.rate: Listed frozen vegetables 0%; others normal rate
0710.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: frozen mushrooms other than Agaricus (0710 80 69) and other frozen vegetables (0710 80 95) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal 14.4%). Frozen potatoes (14.4%) and sweet corn (5.1% + €9.40/100 kg) keep the normal rate.

0711.basis: EU Common Customs Tariff, 2026 (TARIC, origin US). Not in the 2026/1455 annexes, so the normal rate applies; check TARIC for the exact CN line.

0712.rate: Dried onions and most dried vegetables 0%
0712.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: dried onions (0712 20 00) and other dried vegetables and mixtures (0712 90 90) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal rate 12.8%).

0713.basis: EU Common Customs Tariff, 2026 (TARIC, origin US): dried peas (0713 10 90), chickpeas (0713 20 00), kidney and other beans (0713 33 90) and lentils (0713 40 00) are duty-free for U.S. goods.

0714.basis: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex I: fresh, whole sweet potatoes for human consumption (0714 20 10) 0% from July 1, 2026 (normal rate 3%).

profile.headline: The EU buys mainly dry beans, chickpeas and lentils, which enter at its 0% normal rate, and sweet potatoes, mostly through the Netherlands. Since July 1, 2026 U.S. onions, fresh sweet potatoes, asparagus, sweet peppers, fresh beans and several dried and frozen vegetables are duty-free too, but EU plant-health rules still keep out U.S. potatoes.
profile.mainProducts: Dried beans, peas & lentils (0713) · Cassava, sweet potatoes & other roots (0714)
profile.tariffNow: Pulses free; onions, sweet potatoes and other listed vegetables 0% since July 2026

regulator.name: Member-state plant-health authorities (Regulation (EU) 2016/2031 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072)
regulator.requirement: Fresh vegetables need a USDA phytosanitary certificate and plant-health checks at the EU border. Potato tubers (seed and ware) from the United States are prohibited (Annex VI, entries 15 and 17).

0710.basis: China's normal rate (WITS, 2023: 10–13%); frozen vegetables are not on the 2018 List 1. Frozen sweet corn (0710.40) pays 10% + 10% under Announcement No. 3 of 2019 (Annex 3) + 5% under Announcement No. 4 of 2019 as halved + the extra 10%; other lines carry different 2019 rates (not individually verified).

0711.basis: China's normal rate (WITS, 2023: 13%), plus 2.5% under Announcement No. 4 of 2019 as halved, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025, 24 points suspended to January 10, 2027); other 2018–19 lists not checked line by line.

0712.basis: China's normal rate (WITS, 2023: 13% on most dried vegetables), plus 25% under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 5 of 2018 (List 1, from July 6, 2018), plus 5% under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 4 of 2019 (10% from September 1, 2019, halved from February 14, 2020), plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025, 24 points suspended to January 10, 2027).

0713.rate: Normal rate (5–7.5%) + 25% + 2.5–5% + 10%; dried peas 42.5%, kidney beans 47.5%
0713.basis: China's normal rate (WITS, 2023: dried peas 5%, lentils and chickpeas 7%, kidney beans 7.5%), plus 25% under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 5 of 2018 (List 1, from July 6, 2018), plus 2.5% (peas, lentils, chickpeas) or 5% (kidney beans) under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 4 of 2019 as halved from February 14, 2020, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025, 24 points suspended to January 10, 2027). Pulses are not eligible for China’s exclusion process.

0714.basis: China's normal rate (WITS, 2023: 13% on fresh sweet potatoes), plus 25% under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 5 of 2018 (List 1, from July 6, 2018), plus 5% under Tariff Commission Announcement No. 4 of 2019 (10% from September 1, 2019, halved from February 14, 2020), plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025, 24 points suspended to January 10, 2027).

profile.headline: China bought $50 million in 2025, mostly dried peas, beans and other pulses ($37 million) and frozen vegetables. U.S. pulses pay about 42–48% because China’s 2018 counter-tariff of 25% still applies and pulses cannot get an exclusion; its separate 10% on U.S. farm goods ended on November 10, 2025.
profile.mainProducts: Dried beans, peas & lentils (0713) · Frozen vegetables (0710)

regulator.name: General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)
regulator.requirement: Fresh vegetables are admitted only under an APHIS–GACC protocol; plants that pack dried beans and dried or frozen vegetables for China must be registered with GACC, and each lot needs a USDA phytosanitary certificate.

profile.headline: U.S. sales to India fell from $80.6 million in 2024 to $6.7 million in 2025, almost all pulses. Since November 1, 2025 yellow peas from every country pay 30%, after nearly two years duty-free, and the February 2026 U.S.–India framework does not name pulses.
profile.mainProducts: Dried beans, peas & lentils (0713) · Dried vegetables (0712)

regulator.name: Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine & Storage (PPQS) and FSSAI
regulator.requirement: An import permit under India’s Plant Quarantine (Regulation of Import into India) Order, 2003 and a USDA phytosanitary certificate; FSSAI clears food at the port. Yellow pea imports must also be registered in India’s online Import Monitoring System.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: India import requirements

assumptions: Rates are each market's 2026 schedule: Canada's and Mexico's USMCA schedules, the EU Common Customs Tariff (TARIC, November 2026) with Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Japan's Tariff Schedule of October 31, 2026 (including its Japan–U.S. Trade Agreement column), the UK Global Tariff, Taiwan's customs import tariff (column 1), CAFTA-DR for the Dominican Republic and Costa Rica, China's normal rates as reported to WITS (2023) with its additional duties, and India's customs notifications.

Each cell names the products that carry most of the trade in that group; other lines in the same heading can pay a different rate. Cells marked "not individually verified" are small groups where the rate was not checked line by line.
Trade-agreement rates apply only to goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the EU's 2026 U.S. preferences need proof of U.S. origin, and quota rates apply only while the quota lasts.

China's cells add its 2018–19 counter-tariffs (25% under the 2018 List 1 on fresh and dried vegetables, pulses and roots; 2.5–5% under the 2019 list after the 2020 halving; 10% under the 2019 list on some frozen vegetables) and its extra 10% on all U.S. goods to its normal rate. Only carrots, turnips and radishes (0706) can get a market-based exclusion.
National 8–10-digit lines can set a different rate than the six-digit subheading. Check the market's own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
